 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act',
for short) has been filed by the appellant-petitioner being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 18.12.2019 passed in MVC No.496/2017 by the Prl. District and Sessions Judge, MACT Raichur, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal', for short).

sentences.text: 2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 20.08.2017 at about 10.00 p.m. NC: 2023:KHC-K:7403-DB the injured petitioner along with other villagers were traveling in a Tempo Traveler bearing registration No.KA- 33/A-3089 towards Bengaluru.

When they reached near Balenahalli gate walker Sira-Tumakur NH-48 at about 5.00 a.m., the driver of the said Tempo Traveler started to drive the said vehicle with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life without caring for the inmates of the vehicle and without blowing any horn and lost control over the said tempo and hit against a lorry.
Due to the said heavy impact, petitioner along with other inmates of the vehicle sustained fracture injuries.
Petitioner sustained grievous fracture injury over forehead, face traumatic quadriparesis due to cervical spinal cord injury with C6, C7 anterior translation and on other parts of the body.
He became unconscious and taken to Government Hospital Sira.

He has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- for the medical expenses.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner was doing agricultural work and earning Rs.15,000/-
per NC: 2023:KHC-K:7403-DB month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has been permanently disabled and lost source of income, causing dent to him financially, mentally and physically.
Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed ex-parte.
Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim petition and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 241 documents as Exs.P1 to P241.

On the other hand, respondent No.2-Insurer examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 to R3.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7403-DB 8.

The Tribunal, after recording the evidence and considering the material on record, allowed the petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.27,31,707/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till realization from respondent No.1 and directed the respondent No.2 to deposit the compensation amount.
Being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner has filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation amount.
9. We have heard the learned counsel for appellant/petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
10. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is on the lower side.
It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for the appellant that the tribunal has erred in awarding compensation despite placing on record documents at Exs.P1, P6, P7 to P11 and P13 to 241.

On these grounds learned counsel seeks indulgence of this Court to allow the NC:
2023:KHC-K:7403-DB appeal and consequently seeks to enhance the compensation.
11. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company supports the judgment and award passed by the tribunal, contending that the same does not call for any interference.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.
12. We have perused the records and considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties.
13. The accidental injuries sustained by the petitioner and the liability of Respondent No.2 to pay the compensation is not seriously disputed.
In order to prove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner has produced FIR and charge sheet which are marked as Exs.P1 and 2. Ex.P2.

The same discloses that the accident has occurred due to the rash NC:

sentences.text: Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, the petitioner has contended that prior to the accident he was hale and healthy, aged about 42 years and doing agricultural work and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accident he has suffered permanent disability.
In order to substantiate the same, he has produced the disability certificate issued by the doctor who assessed 100% permanent disability to the petitioner as per Ex.P20.

Further, he has produced Exs.P8 and 10,
wherein he has taken follow up treatment for long time so also Ex.P7, discharge summary wherein,
he was taken treatment as inpatient and it is mentioned that traumatic quadriparesis due to cervical mentioned with C-6, C-7 anterior translation.
The tribunal has computed the disability at 75% to the whole body which is just and proper.
The petitioner has not produced any evidence with regard to his income.
Therefore, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2017, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.10,250/- p.m.

In view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, to the aforesaid amount, 25% has to be added towards future prospects as the petitioner was aged about 42 years.

The Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mohd. Sabeer alias Shabir Hussain Vs. Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Transport Corporation reported in AIR 2023 SC 186 wherein it is held at paragraph No.18 as under:
"18.

sentences.text:
It is well settled position of law that in cases of permanent disablement caused by a motor accident, the claimant is entitled to not just future loss of income, but also future prospects."
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7403-DB 16.
Thus, income of the petitioner being Rs.10,250/- per month i.e., 25% of the said income is added towards further prospects, the monthly income comes to Rs.12,812/.
The multiplier applicable to his age group is '14'.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,14,312/- (Rs.12,812/- x 75% x 12 x 14) on account of 'loss of future earning capacity'.
17.
In view of this Court enhancing the income of the petitioner to Rs.10,250/- per month, requires three months to get back to his normal work.
The loss of income during laid up period comes to Rs.30,750/- (Rs.10,250/- X 3 months).

18. Towards pain and suffering, Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded as against Rs.50,000/- in view of the grievous injury over forehead, face traumatic quadriparesis due to cervical spinal cord injury with C-6, C-7 anterior translation and on other parts of the body.
